comments.content: The base field border uses `--color-rule` (#e5e3e1) on a white sheet: about 1.2:1 contrast, far below the 3:1 that WCAG 1.4.11 requires to identify a control boundary. The border only becomes visible on hover/focus, so an unfocused field is nearly indistinguishable from the page and users with low vision cannot see where to type. Use a token that reaches 3:1 (the existing `--color-ink-3` #736d69 is ~4.6:1, or add a dedicated `--color-rule-input` around #8c8681 for a softer look) so the boundary is identifiable at rest.

`touch-action: none` disables *all* browser touch gestures on the sheet host — panning and pinch-zoom included — which directly contradicts the comment above it ("il browser può ancora fare pan, ma non zoomare il documento"). The JS in UniverSheet.tsx only intercepts two-finger pinch (touchstart/touchmove with `touches.length === 2`); single-finger panning and page scrolling over the sheet are then handled by nobody, so on a phone a tall sheet cannot be scrolled and the surrounding modal cannot be scrolled by dragging over the sheet. Blocking pinch-zoom also removes the browser zoom escape hatch (WCAG 1.4.4/1.4.10). Use `touch-action: pan-x pan-y` (or `manipulation`) so native pan stays available while the pinch handler keeps controlling the sheet zoom.

Screen-reader users lose the current page name and every keyboard hint as soon as the bar tightens. Use the same visually-hidden pattern (`position: absolute; width/height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip-path: inset(50%)`) instead of `display: none`.

`@keyframes reveal` is never referenced anywhere in the file (no `animation: reveal ...`), and the reduced-motion block still disables an animation on `main .mod` that this stylesheet never sets. Either the rule that applied `reveal` was dropped (in which case the documented "moduli visibili subito / rivelazione allo scorrimento" behaviour silently disappeared) or both the keyframes and the reduced-motion override are stale. No code in `frontend/src` ever sets `data-closing`, so `:not([data-closing])` is always true and the guard is dead. This whole `jss_*` skin targets Jspreadsheet CE, which is no longer a dependency (`frontend/package.json` only declares Univer) and no component in `frontend/src` renders a `tabularium-sheet` container. Setting the standard `scrollbar-color`/`scrollbar-width` makes Chrome/Edge (121+) ignore the `::-webkit-scrollbar*` rules below, so the intended 10px track, the `--color-fill` groove and the `::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb:hover` affordance never apply in the primary target browser; only Firefox gets the standard colouring and WebKit-based browsers get the custom scrollbar. Pick one approach — e.g. keep the standard properties and express the hover state with `scrollbar-color` on `:hover`, or drop the standard ones so the webkit rules stay authoritative.

Making the *default* state invisible means the content is only visible if a listener installed in `main.tsx` happens to run and if the `load`/`error` event is caught. Any path where that listener is absent (unit tests with jsdom, a different entry point, a component rendered before the listener, an `` whose `data-fade` attribute is added after the image already completed) leaves the image permanently blank — an invisible failure mode for real thumbnails. Prefer a fail-visible default: e.g. fade only when JS has marked the element as pending (`img[data-fade][data-pending] { opacity: 0 }`) or add an `animation` with a short `forwards` fallback, so a missing `data-loaded` degrades to "shown" instead of "hidden".

def _redact(row: sqlite3.Row) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Hide credentials embedded in the recorded command line."""
    item = dict(row)
    try:
        command = json.loads(item.get("command_json") or "{}")
    except ValueError:
        return item
    argv = command.get("argv")
    if isinstance(argv, list):
        masked: list[str] = []
        hide_next = False
        for arg in argv:
            if hide_next:
                masked.append("***")
                hide_next = False
                continue
            if isinstance(arg, str) and arg in _SECRET_FLAGS:
                masked.append(arg)
                hide_next = True
                continue
            masked.append(arg)
        command["argv"] = masked
        item["command_json"] = json.dumps(command)
    return item

comments.content: The `try` here only guards decoding errors, but `_fernet()` is invoked inside it and raises `RuntimeError` when `TABULARIUM_VAULT_KEY` is not set or `cryptography` is missing. That exception escapes `get()`, so the documented "absent secret" contract (`""`) is broken, and `has()` propagates it too: e.g. `compute_profiles._out()` calls `vault.has(ref)` while serializing every profile, turning a listing into an HTTP 500 whenever the key is unconfigured (only `api/system.py` guards against `RuntimeError`). Either catch the configuration error here or make `has()` degrade to `False`.

Any string that is not a valid Fernet key is silently converted into a key with a single, unsalted SHA-256. Two problems: (1) a malformed/typo'd `TABULARIUM_VAULT_KEY` (e.g. value copied with quotes) never fails fast — secrets get written under an unintended derived key, `unreadable_names()` reports nothing while the typo is in place, and the data becomes unreadable the moment the key is corrected; (2) for a human passphrase this is a fast, unsalted KDF, so a low-entropy key can be brute-forced offline from a stolen `secrets` table. Validate strictly (reject keys that are not valid Fernet keys) or, if passphrases must be supported, derive with PBKDF2/scrypt and a documented salt/iteration count.

`get()` is documented/called as a lookup that returns `""` when the ref does not resolve to a readable secret, but a syntactically invalid ref (e.g. `"vault:"`, `"vault:  "`, or a ref with characters outside `_NAME`) raises `ValueError` out of it. Not every caller guards this: `api/cloud.py::_credential` passes an admin-supplied `credential_ref` straight to `vault.get()`, so a malformed ref yields a 500 instead of a 400/empty result. Return `""` for non-matching refs here (and keep `ValueError` only for `put()`/`delete()`, where the caller controls the name).

The clone is pinned neither to a tag nor to a commit SHA: `--depth 1` on the default branch downloads whatever upstream `main` contains at that moment, and `serve_manager` then executes `parsing/serve.py` from that checkout. A force-push/compromise/compromised release on the remote therefore silently runs unreviewed code on the user's machine, and two machines provisioning on different days get different code. Pin the ref (e.g. `--branch <tag>`) and ideally record/verify the expected commit before executing the checkout.
